origins.title: A merchant household
origins.text: You are born above a small shop near the harbor. Your family sells goods downstairs and sleeps in rooms above it. A relative watches you while the shop is open.

origins.title: A pottery-worker household
origins.text: You are born into a family of pottery workers. Your home shares a courtyard with their workshop. Adults take turns caring for you while clay dries and orders are finished.

origins.title: A quay-laborer household
origins.text: You are born into a family of quay laborers. Your household rents crowded rooms a few streets from the water. Neighbors help with your care when several adults are called to unload a ship.

origins.title: A fishing household
origins.text: You are born near the shore into a family that catches and sells fish. Nets hang outside the doorway. A grandparent cares for you during the early morning trips.

origins.title: A bakery household
origins.text: You are born into a family working in a rented bakery. The ovens are lit before dawn. You sleep in a quieter room with an aunt while the first loaves are made.

origins.title: A clerk's household
origins.text: You are born into a household supported by paid writing and record keeping. Work tablets and documents are kept out of your reach. Your parents share your care with a nearby relative.

origins.title: A weaving household
origins.text: You are born into a household that prepares thread and weaves cloth for customers. Work fills part of the main room. Older relatives care for you while the adults finish orders.

origins.title: Newcomers from the Delta
origins.text: You are born in Alexandria shortly after your family moves from a Delta village. They rent a room with relatives and look for steady city work. Food and childcare are shared while they settle in.

mortality.description: The adult baseline uses 100% of the annual probabilities converted from Zakrzewski (2015), Table 1, after Bagnall and Frier's Roman Egyptian female model. The former discounts at ages 18-94 are removed. Only the comparison bands below 18 retain early-play discounts; childhood still uses the existing causal-health system. In health-enabled lives these adult probabilities calibrate warned serious illness episodes, with a neutral reference of Health 50, household rest/care 0.55 and no family recovery bonus. They are not a second independent death roll. Actual play varies with Health, care, existing conditions and risky choices. This is a later-period female proxy, not observed Ptolemaic Alexandrian mortality. The 95+ tail and within-band annual interpolation remain assumptions; age 100 closes the record without assigning death.

jobs.title: Workshop apprentice
jobs.description: Prepare materials and learn a trade under a craft worker. Your work contributes a small amount to the household while you train.

jobs.title: Quay porter

jobs.title: Potter

jobs.title: Merchant's clerk

jobs.title: Workshop copyist

jobs.title: Merchant sailor

jobs.title: Astrologer

character.deathCauseDescription: Natural deaths name an active illness, injury or physical decline that was recorded before fatal progression. A serious illness can cause a sharp Health decline even in a previously healthy person, followed by a care decision. The adult all-cause baseline comes from the historical comparison; disease labels, severity and treatment response are fictional gameplay, not measured cause-specific rates or retrospective diagnoses. Explicit dangerous choices retain their authored fatal outcomes and record the choice that caused death.

deathCauses.title: Pneumonia
deathCauses.text: Pneumonia makes breathing difficult. Your household cares for you, but the infection worsens and you die.

deathCauses.title: Malaria
deathCauses.text: Malaria causes repeated fever and severe weakness. You do not recover.

deathCauses.title: Dysentery
deathCauses.text: Dysentery causes persistent diarrhoea and dehydration. You grow weaker and die.

deathCauses.title: Tuberculosis

events.title: Fighting in Alexandria
events.text: Caesar arrives in 48 BCE during the struggle for Egypt's throne. Fighting breaks out in Alexandria and reaches streets near the harbor.

events.title: The city's water during the war
events.text: The war continues into 47 BCE. A Roman account describes attempts to cut Caesar's water supply and the digging of wells.

events.title: News from Actium
events.text: News arrives that Antony and Cleopatra's forces lost at Actium in 31 BCE. Octavian now has the advantage in the war.

events.title: Egypt under Roman rule
events.text: Ptolemaic rule ends in 30 BCE and Egypt comes under Roman control. Augustus later lists the addition of Egypt among his achievements.

outcomes.text: You turn down the offer and continue your current work.

events.title: Job offers
events.text: Workshops, merchant crews and local teachers are looking for help. Your skills decide which offers you can take. You can also keep your current work.

choices.text: Take porter work close to home

outcomes.text: You take regular porter work nearby. A few useful contacts help you find more jobs.
You take porter work nearby. The first payments are lower than you expected.

choices.text: Take a sailor's place with the ship's crew

outcomes.text: You join the crew and sail out of the harbor. The work pays, but you spend less time at home.
You join the crew. The first crossing leaves you tired, and other sailors help you learn the tasks.

choices.text: Become a copyist in the workshop

outcomes.text: You start at a copyist's workshop. You copy short passages and check them with another worker.

choices.text: Keep your current job

outcomes.text: You pass on the offers and continue your current job.

choices.text: Make pottery decoration your regular work

outcomes.text: You arrange work as a ceramic decorator and buy a few supplies.

choices.text: Make wood carving your regular work

outcomes.text: You arrange work as a wood carver and buy a few supplies.

choices.text: Make sculpture your regular work

outcomes.text: You arrange work as a sculptor and buy a few supplies.

choices.text: Make teaching philosophy your regular work

outcomes.text: You arrange work as a philosophy tutor and buy a few supplies.

choices.text: Make sky-table work your regular occupation

outcomes.text: You arrange work as a sky-table calculator and buy a few supplies.

choices.text: Make chart reading your regular work

outcomes.text: You arrange work as a astrologer and buy a few supplies.

events.title: A busy week at the family shop
events.text: A relative expects more customers than usual and asks for help. They can pay you for covering the counter or checking deliveries. You can also keep your usual plans.

choices.text: Cover the counter for extra pay

outcomes.text: You serve customers through the busy part of the day and receive 30 drachmas.

choices.text: Check the deliveries and accounts

outcomes.text: You compare the delivered goods with the records. Your relative pays you 10 drachmas and shows you how they keep the accounts.

choices.text: Keep your plans and visit afterward

outcomes.text: Your relative finds someone else to help. You stop by after closing and share a meal.

events.title: A pottery order at home
events.text: The family workshop has an order of plain vessels to finish. Your relatives offer paid preparation work or a chance to learn more careful finishing. Neither option changes your regular occupation.

choices.text: Prepare the clay for 30 drachmas

outcomes.text: You prepare material and clean the benches. The family pays you 30 drachmas for the extra work.

choices.text: Learn to finish the vessels

outcomes.text: You work beside an experienced potter, correcting rims and handles. Most of the time goes into practice.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You cannot fit in the order. You help put the tools away when you visit later.

events.title: An extra unloading shift
events.text: A relative knows a crew that needs help with a delivery. You can carry loads for pay, learn the tally work or turn down the extra shift.

choices.text: Carry the loads for 40 drachmas

outcomes.text: You finish the unloading shift and receive 40 drachmas. It leaves less time for your household that day.

choices.text: Help check the cargo tallies

outcomes.text: You compare marks and quantities with an experienced worker. You earn 10 drachmas while learning the task.

choices.text: Decline the shift and stay home

outcomes.text: You decline the extra work and finish several jobs around the household.

events.title: The family's fish delivery
events.text: Your family has a large catch to sell. They offer you a share for helping at the stall, or you can stay near home and work on the nets.

choices.text: Help sell the catch for 30 drachmas

outcomes.text: You sort baskets and serve customers until the fish are sold. Your share is 30 drachmas.

choices.text: Mend the nets with a relative

outcomes.text: You replace damaged cord and practise the knots that keep the net even.

choices.text: Keep your existing plans

outcomes.text: The family divides the work among the people already available. You visit after the delivery.

events.title: A larger bakery order
events.text: The bakery has accepted a larger order. A relative offers you paid delivery work or a slower session learning how quantities and orders are checked.

choices.text: Deliver the loaves for 30 drachmas

outcomes.text: You make several deliveries and return the baskets. The bakery pays you 30 drachmas.

choices.text: Learn the measurements and order lists

outcomes.text: You compare measures and quantities with a relative, then help check the written orders.

choices.text: Visit after the order is finished

outcomes.text: You keep your usual work and join the family for food after the bakery closes.

events.title: Extra documents at home
events.text: A relative has more documents to prepare than they can finish alone. You can help carry completed pages, practise checking a simple copy or leave them to arrange other help.

choices.text: Deliver the documents for 20 drachmas

outcomes.text: You deliver the pages to the named recipients and bring back acknowledgments. Your relative pays you 20 drachmas.

choices.text: Practise checking a simple copy

outcomes.text: You compare two short copies with a relative. They explain the mistakes you missed.

choices.text: Keep to your own work

outcomes.text: Your relative asks another reader for help. You bring food when you visit in the evening.

events.title: A cloth order to finish
events.text: Your relatives have cloth to prepare for a customer. They offer paid finishing work, or you can spend time learning how the pieces are measured and checked.

choices.text: Help finish the order for 30 drachmas

outcomes.text: You trim loose threads, fold the finished cloth and prepare it for delivery. Your share is 30 drachmas.

choices.text: Practise measuring and checking the cloth

outcomes.text: A relative helps you measure the pieces and find flaws before they are packed.

choices.text: Keep the time for your household

outcomes.text: Your relatives arrange other help. You use the time for repairs and errands at home.

events.title: A delivery for relatives
events.text: Relatives from the Delta need help getting a delivery to a city buyer. They offer a payment for handling the sale, or you can use the visit to learn their delivery records.

choices.text: Help complete the delivery for 30 drachmas

outcomes.text: You meet the buyer, check the delivered goods and return the containers. Your relatives give you 30 drachmas.

choices.text: Help with the delivery records

outcomes.text: A relative explains the measures and marks used for the shipment. You practise checking the quantities.

choices.text: Help host the visiting relatives

outcomes.text: Someone else handles the delivery. You find sleeping space, collect food and spend the evening with the visitors.

events.title: A message home
events.text: A returning sailor can carry a message home. You can pay a writer to help or spend the day looking around the port.

choices.text: Send a long message home

outcomes.text: You send news about the work, the port and the people you have met.

choices.text: Spend the day learning the port

outcomes.text: You walk the quays and find the shops and landing places you need.

events.title: A damaged page
events.text: A damaged page reaches the workshop. An experienced copyist offers to work through it with you, but other paid work is also available.

choices.text: Work beside an experienced copyist

outcomes.text: The copyist shows you how to check the damaged words. You finish part of the page together.

choices.text: Take paid work instead

outcomes.text: You finish the paid task and put the money aside. You leave the damaged page for another day.

events.title: A neighbor needs help
events.text: A neighbor asks you to arrange a small job. You can help for free or agree on a payment.

choices.text: Make time for your neighbor

outcomes.text: You arrange the job without charging. Your neighbor thanks you and offers help in return.

choices.text: Agree on a fair payment

outcomes.text: You agree on a price, arrange the work and receive the payment.

events.title: A traveler needs help
events.text: A traveler asks for help finding work. You can offer a meal, teach a task or introduce them to someone hiring.

choices.text: Share a meal and a little time

outcomes.text: You share food with the traveler and explain where they might find work.

choices.text: Teach something useful

outcomes.text: You demonstrate a useful task and let the traveler try it.

choices.text: Introduce the traveler to someone with work

outcomes.text: You introduce the traveler to someone hiring. They arrange a time to meet.

events.title: An agreement does not add up
events.text: The payment in an agreement is lower than you expected. Someone wants you to accept it quickly.

choices.text: Ask for a careful reading of the agreement

outcomes.text: A reader spots the missing payment before you accept the agreement.

choices.text: Ask someone trusted to help settle it

outcomes.text: A trusted person helps both sides agree on a revised payment.

choices.text: Leave the work and keep your time

outcomes.text: You leave without the payment and spend the time on other tasks.

events.title: Talk of marriage
events.text: Friends mention people you might like to meet. You have room to start a relationship if you want one.

events.title: Family plans
events.text: You and your spouse talk about having a child and how you would share the care.

events.title: A friend asks about work
events.text: A younger friend wants help finding work. You could explain a few tasks or let them work beside you.

choices.text: Explain where to look for work

outcomes.text: You explain where to ask for work and how to handle a few common tasks.

choices.text: Let your friend work beside you

outcomes.text: Your friend works beside you for a while and helps finish an order.

events.title: A poor harvest
events.text: Reports of a poor harvest reach the city. Your household decides whether to store more food or share some supplies with relatives.

choices.text: Keep a small reserve for the household

outcomes.text: You buy a small reserve of food and store it at home.

choices.text: Share with the people closest to you

outcomes.text: You divide some supplies among relatives and keep less for your household.

events.title: New rules for work
events.text: Roman officials have changed some arrangements for work and agreements. You can ask about the new rules or get help from neighbors.

choices.text: Learn how the new arrangements work

outcomes.text: You ask about the new forms and learn which arrangements affect your work.

choices.text: Stay close to your established network

outcomes.text: Neighbors explain the new arrangements and help you find the right person to ask.

events.title: At forty
events.text: You turn forty. You have handled enough jobs and household problems to recognize some of them quickly.

events.title: An older relative needs help
events.text: An older relative needs help with meals and daily tasks. You must fit their care around paid work.

choices.text: Give more of your own time

outcomes.text: You miss some paid work to help your relative with meals and daily tasks.

choices.text: Arrange help across the household

outcomes.text: Several household members agree on times to help with the care.

events.title: Changing your workload
events.text: Carrying and lifting leave you tired for longer. You can take lighter tasks or keep working at the same pace.

choices.text: Take lighter tasks that need experience

outcomes.text: You take lighter tasks that need checking and advice rather than lifting.

choices.text: Keep taking the same jobs

outcomes.text: You keep taking the same jobs and earn more, but need longer to recover afterward.

events.title: Teaching a learner
events.text: A younger worker asks you to teach them. Lessons will take time away from your own orders.

choices.text: Teach the learner

outcomes.text: You show the learner each step and check their first attempts. Your own work takes longer.

choices.text: Finish your own orders

outcomes.text: You finish your own orders and make notes on the parts that need care.

events.title: Taking more rest
events.text: You have been slow to recover after work. You can take more days off or reduce your workload a little.

choices.text: Take more days off

outcomes.text: You take more days off. You earn less and recover some energy.

choices.text: Drop some demanding tasks

outcomes.text: You drop a few demanding tasks and keep the lighter paid work.

events.title: Leaving regular work
events.text: Your regular job is getting harder to manage. Leaving it will reduce your income, so your household will need to adjust.

choices.text: Leave your regular job

outcomes.text: You leave your regular job. You rest more and help with smaller household tasks.

choices.text: Keep some lighter work

outcomes.text: You keep some regular work and turn down the heavier tasks.

events.title: Arranging your belongings
events.text: You decide who should receive your belongings and settle your remaining obligations. You can record the arrangements or discuss them at home.

choices.text: Have the arrangements written down

outcomes.text: You pay for your instructions about belongings and obligations to be recorded.

choices.text: Discuss the arrangements at home

outcomes.text: You tell the household who should receive your belongings and how to settle your obligations.

events.title: Sorting papers and letters
events.text: You have a little time to help a younger person or sort the letters and papers you have kept.

choices.text: Show a beginner how to do a task

outcomes.text: You show a beginner how to handle a task and correct their first attempt.

choices.text: Sort your letters

outcomes.text: You sort your letters and label the ones you want to keep.

events.title: A visitor calls
events.text: A familiar visitor sits with you for a while. You can tell them a story or ask for their news.

choices.text: Tell a story about an old job

outcomes.text: You tell your visitor about an old job and answer a few questions.

choices.text: Ask for the visitor's news

outcomes.text: Your visitor tells you about work and the people at home.

events.title: An afternoon at home
events.text: You have a free afternoon. You can rest outside or ask someone to visit.

choices.text: Rest outside

outcomes.text: You sit outside for a while and return indoors when you get tired.

choices.text: Invite someone to visit

outcomes.text: A visitor joins you for a drink and stays through the afternoon.

events.title: An old neighbor's name
events.text: You mention an old neighbor. Someone asks where they lived, and you describe the house.

events.title: More help at home
events.text: At ninety, you need more help with meals, washing and moving around the house.

events.title: Your ninety-fifth year
events.text: You turn ninety-five. Your household helps with most daily tasks and makes sure you have company.

events.title: Resting at home
events.text: You spend much of the day resting. Someone brings water and leaves the door open for air.

events.title: A letter from a friend
events.text: A friend sends news from another town. You can pay to send a reply or put the letter aside for now.

choices.text: Send a reply

outcomes.text: You send a reply with your news and a few questions.

choices.text: Keep the message for another day

outcomes.text: You store the letter and leave the reply for another day.

events.title: An unwell week
events.text: You are still recovering from an illness or injury. Everyday tasks take longer, and some work has to wait.

events.title: Recognizing voices
events.text: You recognize the people who care for you and turn when they call. They repeat the same names and songs through the day.

events.title: At the doorway
events.text: You watch people pass the doorway. An adult brings you back inside whenever you wander too far.

events.title: Meals and naps
events.text: Your caregivers fit meals and naps around their work. You object loudly when a meal is late.

events.title: More words
events.text: You learn a few more words and use them to ask for food, water and familiar people.

events.title: Sitting in the shade
events.text: Someone moves your seat out of the sun. You watch people carry baskets through the courtyard.

events.title: A familiar visitor
events.text: You recognize a visitor and reach toward them. They stop to talk and carry you for a while.

events.title: Knowing the way
events.text: You learn a shorter route to a nearby shop. You get there and back before the household starts looking for you.

events.title: Helping with small jobs
events.text: You carry small items, clear dishes and repeat messages. Adults still check the jobs before letting you go.

events.title: A smooth stone
events.text: You find a smooth stone and keep it in a pouch. Another child offers to trade for it, but you keep it.

events.title: A running joke
events.text: A friend makes everyone laugh during a game. You keep repeating the joke until the adults ask you to stop.

events.title: Trying a task
events.text: An adult lets you try part of a familiar task. They correct your grip and help you finish.

events.title: A longer errand
events.text: An errand takes you farther from home than usual. You find the right doorway and return with the delivery done.

events.title: More to do
events.text: You take on a few more tasks this year. An experienced worker checks the parts you are still learning.

events.title: Practice at work
events.text: A task takes several tries. Someone shows you where it went wrong, and you try again.

events.title: Work and expenses
events.text: People at home discuss work and the cost of supplies. You help check what needs doing tomorrow.

events.title: Different working hours
events.text: Your friends start keeping different working hours. You arrange to meet when everyone is free.

events.title: Delivering a message
events.text: Someone sends you with a message. You repeat it on the way so you will not forget part of it.

events.title: Asking about jobs
events.text: You ask workers how they learned their jobs. Some offer advice; others are too busy to stop.

events.title: The walk to work
events.text: You take the usual route to your job. A blocked lane makes you walk around the market on the way home.

events.title: Repairing a worn item
events.text: You repair a worn household item instead of replacing it. The repair holds after a few adjustments.

events.title: A long meal
events.text: Visitors stay after a meal to exchange news. You clear the dishes later than planned.

events.title: A busy week
events.text: Several jobs and household tasks need doing at once. You finish the urgent ones and leave the rest for later.

events.title: An hour off
events.text: You finish a task early and sit outside for a while. A neighbor stops to ask how the work went.

events.title: Asked to help again
events.text: Someone you helped before asks for another job. They give your name to a neighbor who also needs help.

events.title: Spotting a mistake
events.text: You notice a mistake before it causes more work. You show a younger worker what to check next time.

events.title: Starting later
events.text: You start a heavy task later and take an extra break. It is finished before evening.

events.title: A worker's suggestion
events.text: A younger worker suggests a different way to arrange a task. You try it and keep the part that saves time.

events.title: Moving things around
events.text: Your household moves bedding and storage jars to free some space. Everyone has to learn where things are now.

events.title: A delayed order
events.text: An order is delayed for several days. You work on smaller tasks until the materials arrive.

events.title: Meeting an old acquaintance
events.text: You meet someone you have not seen for years. You exchange news about work and people you both know.

events.title: An afternoon visitor
events.text: A visitor tells you about their household and stays for a drink. You ask them to come again next week.

events.title: Sorting a storage box
events.text: You sort a box of old belongings. Some are still useful, and some need cleaning or repair.

events.title: Help with a task
events.text: Someone offers to carry something that has become difficult for you. You let them take it and explain where it belongs.

events.title: News from the street
events.text: A visitor reports that a shop nearby has changed hands. You ask who is running it now.

events.title: Telling an old story
events.text: You tell a story about an old job. A listener asks a question, and you stop to explain the missing part.

events.title: Moving your chair
events.text: The sun reaches your usual seat earlier this season. Someone moves the chair into the shade.

events.title: News from another port
events.text: Someone mentions a port where you once worked. You ask whether the landing place is still used.

events.title: Checking some writing
events.text: You notice an unclear line on a page. You ask the writer to read it back before anyone copies it.

events.title: Greetings in the street
events.text: You stop several times on a short errand because neighbors want to talk. The errand takes longer than expected.

events.title: Sharing household tasks
events.text: You and your spouse divide the week's household tasks. One of you swaps a task to fit around paid work.

events.title: Your child needs different help
events.text: One of your children brings you a problem you have not handled before. You ask a few questions and work out how to help.

events.title: A friend needs help
events.text: A friend cannot finish a task. You can help, explain how to do it or return to your game.

choices.text: Stay and help

outcomes.text: You help your friend finish the task before returning to play.

choices.text: Show them what you know, then return to play

outcomes.text: You explain the next step and leave your friend to try it.

events.title: A free afternoon
events.text: There is no errand waiting this afternoon. You can watch a worker or find the other children.

choices.text: Watch how something is made

outcomes.text: A worker shows you the tools and answers your questions.

choices.text: Find the other children

outcomes.text: You find the other children and spend the afternoon playing.

events.title: An extra task
events.text: Someone offers you an extra task for a small payment. You had planned to meet people during the same hours.

choices.text: Try the unfamiliar work

outcomes.text: You complete the unfamiliar task and collect a small payment.

choices.text: Keep the time you promised to others

outcomes.text: You turn down the task and meet the people who were expecting you.

events.title: A question about work
events.text: You are stuck on part of a task. An experienced worker has time to explain it if you ask.

choices.text: Ask the question openly

outcomes.text: The worker explains the step you missed. Your next attempt goes better.

choices.text: Watch carefully before trying again

outcomes.text: You watch another attempt and practise the part that gave you trouble.

events.title: Lending a tool
events.text: A neighbor asks to borrow a tool you also need. You could rearrange your work or agree on a time to use it together.

choices.text: Lend it and rearrange your tasks

outcomes.text: Your neighbor returns the tool. You finish your own work later than planned.

choices.text: Offer a time when you can use it together

outcomes.text: You and your neighbor agree on a time to use the tool together.

events.title: Extra paid work
events.text: A small paid job is available. Taking it will leave less time for household tasks.

choices.text: Take the work this time

outcomes.text: You finish the job and bring home the payment. The household tasks wait.

choices.text: Keep the time for home

outcomes.text: You turn down the payment and finish the tasks at home.

events.title: Trying another method
events.text: Someone suggests a different way to finish a task. Trying it will take time and some material.

choices.text: Give the new method a careful try

outcomes.text: You try the new method and keep the steps that save work.

choices.text: Use the method you know well

outcomes.text: You use the method you know and finish without wasting material.

events.title: An invitation
events.text: An acquaintance invites you to a gathering. You could go or visit an old friend instead.

choices.text: Accept the invitation

outcomes.text: You meet several people at the gathering and exchange news about work.

choices.text: Make time for an old friend

outcomes.text: You visit your old friend and stay for a meal.

events.title: Two tasks at once
events.text: Someone asks for advice while you are finishing a task. You have enough energy to do one of them today.

choices.text: Help with the question

outcomes.text: You put your task aside and explain how you would handle the problem.

choices.text: Finish your task first

outcomes.text: You finish your task and arrange to talk another day.

events.title: A question about an old place
events.text: A visitor asks about a place where you once lived. You can describe it or ask someone to write down the details.

choices.text: Describe the place

outcomes.text: You describe the place and answer questions about who lived there.

choices.text: Have the details written down

outcomes.text: Someone writes down the place names and details you want to keep.

events.title: A short outing
events.text: Someone offers to walk with you on a short visit. You could go or invite a visitor to come to your home.

choices.text: Go together, at an easy pace

outcomes.text: You make the short visit, take a break and return home together.

choices.text: Invite a visitor to come to you

outcomes.text: You stay at home and ask your visitor to come over instead.

events.title: An item you no longer use
events.text: You find an item you seldom use. Someone else could use it, but you might still want to keep it.

choices.text: Give the item away

outcomes.text: You give the item to someone who can use it.

choices.text: Keep it for your own use

outcomes.text: You keep the item and explain when you still use it.

events.title: Porridge on the floor
events.text: You knock over your bowl. Someone cleans the floor and gives you a smaller serving.

events.title: A patched blanket
events.text: A relative patches your blanket. You pull at the new stitching until they move your hand.

events.title: A noisy visitor
events.text: A visitor makes you laugh by copying animal sounds. You keep asking for the goat again.

events.title: A chipped cup
events.text: You chip a cup while clearing a meal. An adult shows you how to carry fewer things at once.

events.title: The missing goat
events.text: A neighbor's goat gets loose. You spot it chewing a basket and call for its owner.

events.title: Counting the change
events.text: You bring home the right change from an errand. Your household lets you check the coins yourself.

events.title: Pigeons on the roof
events.text: You and a friend watch pigeons crowd around a rooftop. The owner comes out and chases them away.

events.title: A queue at the bakery
events.text: The bakery opens late. You wait with the other customers and get home after your household expected you.

events.title: A borrowed writing tablet
events.text: A neighbor lends you a tablet for an afternoon. You copy a short list and wipe it clean before returning it.

events.title: A cart blocks the lane
events.text: A cart loses a wheel in a narrow lane. You help shift its baskets so people can get past.

events.title: Dearer bread
events.text: Bread costs more at your usual stall. You buy a smaller loaf and add beans to the meal.

events.title: Cloudy water
events.text: The water in a household jar looks dirty. You empty it, scrub the jar and fetch another load.

events.title: A missing tool
events.text: You spend a morning looking for a tool. It turns up under a folded cloth where you left it.

events.title: A leak after rain
events.text: Rain gets through a crack in the roof. You move a basket and patch the gap before the next shower.

events.title: Waiting at the quay
events.text: Several ships arrive together. The quay stays crowded while porters argue over where to put the cargo.

events.title: A loose hinge
events.text: A door scrapes the floor. You tighten its fittings and ask someone to lift it while you check the gap.

events.title: Checking a measure
events.text: A seller's grain measure looks smaller than yours. You compare them before agreeing on the price.

events.title: A late payment
events.text: Someone pays you later than agreed. You spend less for a few days until the money arrives.

events.title: Mended sandals
events.text: A strap comes loose from your sandal. A neighbor repairs it while you wait nearby.

events.title: A better seat
events.text: A visitor brings a low stool so you can sit outside more comfortably. You return it after the afternoon meal.

events.title: The key turns up
events.text: You cannot find a small key. After checking the room twice, you find it inside a bowl.

events.title: A short visit
events.text: A relative walks with you to a nearby temple. You rest in the shade before heading home.

events.title: A coin in the dust
events.text: You find a coin where a seller has just packed up. They are still close enough to call.

choices.text: Call the seller back

outcomes.text: The seller thanks you and checks the rest of the purse.

choices.text: Take the coin home

outcomes.text: You bring the coin home. Nobody comes looking for it.

events.title: A broken clay toy
events.text: A toy breaks during a game. You can try to mend it or ask the other children to play something else.

choices.text: Try to mend it

outcomes.text: The toy looks crooked, but the pieces hold together.

choices.text: Start another game

outcomes.text: You leave the pieces aside and get everyone playing again.

events.title: An errand across town
events.text: A trader offers a small payment for a delivery. It will take most of the afternoon.

choices.text: Take the delivery

outcomes.text: You get the parcel there on time and collect your payment.

choices.text: Keep your afternoon free

outcomes.text: The trader finds someone else. You spend the afternoon with friends.

events.title: A cheap used tool
events.text: A worker offers to sell you an old tool. It needs cleaning, but it could be useful for practice.

choices.text: Buy and repair it

outcomes.text: You clean the tool and replace a worn fitting before using it.

choices.text: Borrow one when you need it

outcomes.text: A neighbor agrees to lend you a tool for short tasks.

events.title: Space at a market stall
events.text: A seller has room on a stall for a few extra goods. You can pay for the space or help carry the stock instead.

choices.text: Pay for space and sell a small batch

outcomes.text: Some goods sell quickly and some come home with you.

choices.text: Help the seller for a day's pay

outcomes.text: You carry stock, pack the stall and receive the agreed payment.

events.title: Work next door
events.text: A neighbor starts noisy repairs before sunrise. You have a long day ahead and want more sleep.

choices.text: Ask them to start later

outcomes.text: You agree on quieter hours for the next few mornings.

choices.text: Move your sleeping place for now

outcomes.text: You shift your bedding to a quieter corner until the repairs finish.

events.title: Smoke from a warehouse
events.text: Smoke comes from a warehouse doorway. Someone inside calls for help. Going through the smoke could kill you; people outside are forming a bucket line.

choices.text: Stay outside and pass water

outcomes.text: You pass buckets while others clear the nearby buildings.

choices.text: Go inside to help — risk of death

outcomes.text: You reach the person and help them out. You spend days coughing after the smoke.
Heat forces you back. Burns keep you away from work while others care for you.
Carbon monoxide from the fire smoke makes you collapse before you reach the warehouse door. You do not survive the poisoning.

events.title: A rough crossing
events.text: Bad weather is approaching. The master offers extra pay to sail now, but the crew could wait in port. Leaving in this weather could be fatal.

choices.text: Wait in port

outcomes.text: The ship stays moored until the weather improves. You lose the extra payment.

choices.text: Sail for extra pay — risk of death

outcomes.text: The crossing is rough, but the ship reaches port. You collect the extra pay and need a long rest.
A wave sweeps you overboard during the crossing. You drown before the crew can reach you.

events.title: Robbers in a narrow lane
events.text: Two people block your path and demand your purse. You can hand it over and leave. Trying to fight them could be fatal.

choices.text: Hand over the purse and leave

outcomes.text: They take the purse and let you go. You reach home unhurt.

choices.text: Try to fight them — risk of death

outcomes.text: You shout and push past them. Other people arrive before they can follow.
One of the robbers stabs you in the abdomen. Blood loss from the wound proves fatal.

events.title: Water in a dirty jar
events.text: Your stored water smells wrong. Replacing it will cost time and money. Drinking it could cause a serious, sometimes fatal illness.

choices.text: Empty the jar and fetch fresh water

outcomes.text: You scrub the jar and replace the water before the next meal.

choices.text: Use it anyway — risk of fatal illness

outcomes.text: You use the water and notice no illness afterward.
You develop dysentery after drinking the stored water. Diarrhoea and dehydration stop you working, and you need care.
After drinking the stored water, you develop dysentery with severe dehydration. You do not recover.

events.title: A repair overhead
events.text: A roof tile is loose. A worker can repair it, or a relative can help you arrange a cheaper patch from inside.

choices.text: Pay a worker to fix it

outcomes.text: The worker secures the tile and checks the tiles beside it.

choices.text: Ask for help with an inside patch

outcomes.text: You and a relative stop the drip until a full repair can be made.

events.title: Vegetables to prepare
events.text: A neighbor brings vegetables to prepare for a meal. You could help with the cutting or contribute some ingredients.

choices.text: Help prepare the meal

outcomes.text: You sit together and finish the vegetables before the pot is ready.

choices.text: Contribute ingredients instead

outcomes.text: You add a few things from your stores and rest while the others cook.

events.title: A potter at the workshop
events.text: While collecting a repaired jar, you meet Demetria, a potter. You talk while she finishes the handle and learn that she works nearby.

events.title: A conversation at the market
events.text: You meet Thais while buying supplies at the market. She is a trader and helps you compare two sellers' prices.

events.title: Help with a linen order
events.text: A linen order brings you to Berenike's workshop. She helps sort out the measurements, and you spend a little time talking after the work is done.

events.title: Waiting for a copied document
events.text: While waiting for a document, you meet Tyche, a copyist. She explains a missing line and asks where your household lives.

events.title: Checking a kiln load
events.text: You inspect a cooled kiln load. A few pieces are cracked; the rest can be finished for sale.

events.title: A fitting that works
events.text: A repaired wooden fitting holds when you test it. The customer asks you to make another.

events.title: A customer changes the design
events.text: A customer asks for another detail on a small figure. It will take extra time and material.

choices.text: Agree on extra pay and add the detail

outcomes.text: You agree on the price, revise the figure and finish later than planned.

choices.text: Finish the original order

outcomes.text: You finish the design that was agreed and deliver it on time.

events.title: An objection at a discussion
events.text: Someone challenges a claim you have made. They ask you to show how you reached it.

choices.text: Explain the steps and accept questions

outcomes.text: You explain the steps. A question exposes a gap, and you revise part of the argument.

choices.text: Write down the objection and review it later

outcomes.text: You record the objection and compare it with the text after the meeting.

events.title: A clear night
events.text: The sky clears after several cloudy evenings. You add an observation to your record and compare it with the last entry.

events.title: Two different chart readings
events.text: Two readers give different interpretations of the same sky diagram. You can compare their calculations or ask how they chose their rules.

choices.text: Check the positions and arithmetic

outcomes.text: You find a copied position that differs between the charts and record the correction.

choices.text: Compare the interpretation rules

outcomes.text: You list the rules each reader used. The exercise records their beliefs without proving either prediction.

events.title: Orders during the Alexandrian War
events.text: Fighting has reached Alexandria. Your unit needs people to protect stores and a smaller group for a forward post. The forward post carries a risk of death.

choices.text: Guard the stores and move supplies

outcomes.text: You guard the stores and help move supplies away from a threatened lane.

choices.text: Volunteer for the forward post (risk of death)

outcomes.text: You return from the post with a damaged shield and a better understanding of the unit's movements.
A spear strikes your abdomen while you hold the forward post. Blood loss from the wound proves fatal.

events.title: The unit checks its equipment
events.text: During the continuing fighting, your unit guards a storehouse. You check equipment and count incoming supply loads.

events.title: Your first unit orders
events.text: You write a guard rota, check the equipment list and explain the next day's tasks to your unit.

events.title: A command decision about supplies
events.text: Your staff cannot provide the same escort for every route. You must decide whether to protect the district's grain stores or escort the next supply convoy.

choices.text: Assign troops to protect the grain stores

outcomes.text: Your troops take posts at the stores. Clerks report that deliveries can be unloaded there without interruption.

choices.text: Assign troops to escort the supply convoy

outcomes.text: Your escort brings the convoy through. Other units receive their loads on the planned day.

events.title: The new grain order is carried out
events.text: Clerks use the schedule you proposed. Grain is delivered to the district storehouses you named, and the delivery lists are checked against your plan.

events.title: Your royal appointment ends
events.text: Roman rule replaces the Ptolemaic administration. Your royal army or court appointment ends. You keep your training and contacts, but must find other work.

events.title: Comparing a temple sky diagram
events.text: A copied sky diagram is brought for study. You compare its zodiacal signs with other notes and record the differences. Access to this copy is part of the fictional story.

events.title: Care is needed
events.text: An illness or injury is affecting your health. You and the people caring for you must decide what extra help to arrange.

choices.text: Rest and ask for help

outcomes.text: The household makes time for rest and helps with water, food and everyday tasks. Recovery is not certain.

choices.text: Consult a healer for 10 drachmas

outcomes.text: You arrange a healer's visit and set aside time for care. The visit does not guarantee recovery.

choices.text: Keep the usual routine

outcomes.text: The household keeps to its usual routine without arranging extra care. Your health suffers.

events.title: Time to talk
events.text: You and your spouse argue over work, time and household responsibilities. You need to decide what to do.

choices.text: Listen and arrange a meal together

outcomes.text: You discuss what has been difficult and agree on a few changes at home.

choices.text: Set aside time to talk

outcomes.text: You put other tasks aside and talk through the household responsibilities together.

choices.text: Agree to end the marriage

outcomes.text: You agree to separate and divide the household belongings. Your children and their other-parent records remain.

events.title: A petition needs a writer
events.text: A local clerk needs help checking names and explaining a petition. Good work could earn a recommendation for service with royal officials.

choices.text: Help prepare the petition

outcomes.text: You check the names, rewrite the request and answer the clerk's questions. The clerk agrees to recommend you. You still need the skills and age required for a court appointment.

weightModifiers.reason: Your household knows written accounts
Practised writing
Experience explaining requests
Your current work uses written records
You have presented a district petition
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder

outcomes.text: The clerk corrects several passages and files the petition. No recommendation follows. You are paid for the copying.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: The unit's supply lists
events.text: Your unit's equipment and supply lists need checking. You can offer to sort the records and explain the shortages to an officer.

choices.text: Take charge of the supply lists

outcomes.text: The records match the stores, and your officer accepts the revised list. They agree to recommend you for more responsibility. This helps future applications; it does not change your rank.

weightModifiers.reason: Household experience with lists and accounts
You can check supply totals
You understand the unit's equipment
You can explain the shortages
You have wartime supply experience
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder

outcomes.text: You find missing entries, but another soldier has to help finish the count. You return to ordinary duties with more practice.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: A reader checks your calculations
events.text: An experienced reader is checking copied sky tables for a paying household. You can show your own work and ask to help with the next set.

choices.text: Show your copied tables and calculations

outcomes.text: The reader checks your arithmetic and offers to recommend you to the paying household. A regular post is open once you meet its skill requirements. You keep your current work until you accept it.

weightModifiers.reason: Household experience with writing and accounts
You have practised sky-table work
Your arithmetic is well practised
Your current work involves written records
You have completed a paid sky-table copy
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder

outcomes.text: The reader points out a copied position and a calculation to correct. There is no work offer, but you leave with useful corrections.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: An order for a larger household
events.text: A customer is looking for someone who can finish a larger workshop order and organise the smaller tasks. You can show a sample of your pottery, carving or sculpture.

choices.text: Show a finished piece and explain the work

outcomes.text: The customer accepts your sample and recommends you to a workshop owner. You can apply to lead work in your trained trade once you meet the requirements. You keep your current job for now.

weightModifiers.reason: Your household has workshop contacts
You have an experienced specialism
You already work in a skilled workshop
You have completed a paid craft order
You can explain quantities and costs
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder

outcomes.text: The customer asks for a different finish and places the larger order elsewhere. You correct the sample and sell it as an ordinary piece.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: A moneylender offers cash
events.text: A moneylender offers ready cash on the stated repayment terms. This loan is paid manually. Missing the deadline can lead to threats, assault or death.

choices.text: Turn down the loan

outcomes.text: You turn down the loan. You owe this lender nothing.

choices.text: Borrow from the moneylender — dangerous loan

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's cash and repayment terms. You must pay this loan yourself. If it stays unpaid after the deadline, the collectors can threaten, injure or kill you.

events.title: Your loan is due
events.text: The moneylender asks for the remaining balance. Leaving it unpaid can bring threats and, after a longer delay, a dangerous confrontation.

choices.text: Pay the remaining balance

outcomes.text: You pay the remaining balance. The lender marks the loan settled. You owe them nothing.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas toward the loan

outcomes.text: You pay 10 drachmas toward the loan. The remaining balance keeps its existing deadline.

choices.text: Ask for an extension

outcomes.text: The lender adds the agreed extension charge to the balance and gives you a new deadline.

choices.text: Leave the loan unpaid for now

outcomes.text: You leave the balance unpaid. The deadline has not changed, and the collectors may return.

events.title: Collectors at your door
events.text: Two collectors demand payment. They threaten to hurt you if you keep delaying. The balance and deadline remain in force.

choices.text: Pay the remaining balance

outcomes.text: You pay the remaining balance. The lender marks the loan settled. You owe them nothing.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas toward the loan

outcomes.text: You pay 10 drachmas toward the loan. The remaining balance keeps its existing deadline.

choices.text: Ask for an extension

outcomes.text: The lender adds the agreed extension charge to the balance and gives you a new deadline.

choices.text: Leave the loan unpaid for now

outcomes.text: You leave the balance unpaid. The deadline has not changed, and the collectors may return.

events.title: The collectors corner you
events.text: The loan has been overdue for years. Collectors stop you on your way home and threaten violence. Refusing or trying to run can be fatal.

choices.text: Pay the remaining balance

outcomes.text: You pay the remaining balance. The lender marks the loan settled. You owe them nothing.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas toward the loan

outcomes.text: You pay 10 drachmas toward the loan. The remaining balance keeps its existing deadline.

choices.text: Ask for an extension

outcomes.text: The lender adds the agreed extension charge to the balance and gives you a new deadline.

choices.text: Ask the neighbors to speak for you

outcomes.text: Neighbors speak with the collectors. They leave without hurting you, but the balance remains overdue.

weightModifiers.reason: People nearby are willing to speak for you
You can explain your request clearly

outcomes.text: The collectors shove your neighbors aside and beat you before leaving. You are hurt, and the loan remains unpaid.
A collector strikes your lower leg. You suffer an open tibial fracture and need care. The loan remains unpaid.

choices.text: Try to get past them and run

outcomes.text: You get past the collectors and reach a crowded street. You escape for now, but the loan is still overdue.
A collector catches you and strikes your lower leg. You suffer an open tibial fracture and need care.
A collector stabs you in the chest as you try to pass. The wound proves fatal.

choices.text: Refuse to pay or go with them

outcomes.text: The collectors beat you and leave. You are badly hurt, and the loan remains overdue.
The collectors strike your lower leg. An open tibial fracture stops you walking, and you need care.
A collector stabs you in the chest during the confrontation. The wound proves fatal.

events.title: A different sleeping place
events.text: Your household moves your sleeping basket away from a draft. You wake in the unfamiliar corner and cry until someone picks you up.

events.title: Across the mat
events.text: You cross a mat toward the doorway. An adult moves a basket out of your path and calls you back from the street.

events.title: A lid on the floor
events.text: Someone leaves a pot lid within reach. You bang it against the floor until the cook trades it for a wooden spoon.

events.title: The cat keeps its distance
events.text: You reach for a cat resting near the wall. It moves out of reach and watches you from a shelf.

events.title: Supper on a lap
events.text: A relative keeps you on their lap through supper. You take food from their bowl and fall asleep before the dishes are cleared.

events.title: A cloth to hold
events.text: While someone washes you, they let you hold the clean cloth. You drop it into the water and laugh at the splash.

events.title: Waiting out the rain
events.text: Rain keeps the household indoors. Someone moves a basket so you have room to crawl while the adults finish their work.

events.title: A bark at the door
events.text: A dog barks outside the doorway. You hurry back to a familiar adult and watch it from behind their legs.

events.title: A restless night
events.text: You will not settle to sleep. The adults take turns carrying you until the room finally becomes quiet.

events.title: Stones in a bowl
events.text: A relative gives you a bowl and a few smooth stones. You move them in and out while they keep count aloud.

events.title: Sandals that slip
events.text: Your household fits a pair of small sandals to your feet. You keep kicking one off, and someone keeps putting it back.

events.title: Behind the hanging cloth
events.text: An older child hides behind a hanging cloth and calls your name. You pull the edge aside each time they disappear.

events.title: Holding the cup
events.text: Someone helps you drink from a small cup. Most reaches your mouth, and the rest runs down the front of your clothes.

events.title: An afternoon with a relative
events.text: The usual carer has an errand. A relative looks after you, learning which song and which toy will keep you settled.

events.title: Two similar baskets
events.text: You bring home the wrong basket from an errand. An adult goes back with you, and the shopkeeper swaps it for the right one.

events.title: A game with seeds
events.text: Children mark a game on the ground and use seeds as counters. You argue over a move, erase the lines and start again.

events.title: A scrap sail
events.text: You tie a scrap of cloth to a stick and float it in a shallow basin. The little boat tips over as soon as you let go.

events.title: Under the bench
events.text: A chick slips into the room. You crouch under a bench to catch it while its owner waits at the door.

events.title: Pits to sort
events.text: After a meal, you sort olive pits into neat rows. Someone sweeps them into a bowl before the next task can begin.

events.title: A faded doorway mark
events.text: You use a mark on a wall to remember a turning. When the wall is patched, you have to learn another way to recognize the street.

events.title: The bread is still warm
events.text: You carry a loaf home wrapped in cloth. You keep switching hands because the bread is hotter than you expected.

events.title: A strap comes loose
events.text: The strap on a small jug slips from its knot. You set the jug down and wait for someone to retie it before carrying on.

events.title: A shelf to clear
events.text: An adult asks you to clear the bottom shelf of a storeroom. You find a missing spoon behind the jars.

events.title: Getting the words wrong
events.text: You try to join a song in the courtyard. Another child quietly teaches you the words you keep missing.

events.title: Following the shade
events.text: You trace the edge of a building's shade on the ground. Later, you come back and find the line has moved.

events.title: A bead in the dust
events.text: A loose bead rolls between the floor stones. You work it out with a thin stick and return it to its owner.

events.title: Watching the scales
events.text: You stand beside an adult while a seller weighs a purchase. On the way home, they explain why they watched both sides of the scales.

events.title: Remembering a visitor's name
events.text: A visitor asks if you remember them. You remember the food they brought last time, but need help with the name.

events.title: Before the street fills
events.text: You leave early to finish an errand before the street gets busy. The shop has not opened, so you wait with the other early arrivals.

events.title: A knot that holds
events.text: Someone checks the knot on a bundle you tied. They undo it, show you another turn and ask you to try again.

events.title: Two people with the same name
events.text: You deliver a message to the wrong person with the right name. They point you toward the other household before you walk away.

events.title: A handle needs wrapping
events.text: A tool handle is rubbing your palm. You wrap it with a strip of cloth and finish the small job more comfortably.

events.title: A late supper
events.text: A task runs past the meal hour. Your household saves a portion and asks what kept you when you finally arrive.

events.title: Remembering the price
events.text: You repeat the agreed price while walking to make a purchase. At the stall, you remember it but have to count the coins twice.

events.title: Carrying it together
events.text: A bundle is awkward rather than heavy. Another young worker takes the far end, and the two of you get it through the doorway.

events.title: The yard fills again
events.text: You finish sweeping a work yard just before a delivery arrives. Loose packing covers the clean ground, and you fetch the broom again.

events.title: A contest with no prize
events.text: A group challenges each other to balance a pebble on a narrow post. Nobody manages it for long, and no money changes hands.

events.title: Keeping an offcut
events.text: A worker lets you keep a small offcut after clearing the bench. You bring it home and use it to wedge a loose shutter.

events.title: Checking before leaving
events.text: You return to check a delivery before leaving the yard. One item is missing, and you find it where the cart was unloaded.

events.title: A message over the noise
events.text: You try to call a message across a noisy street. Nobody hears the whole thing, so you walk over and say it again.

events.title: The lamp goes out
events.text: The lamp runs out of oil in the middle of an evening task. You leave the last part until daylight.

events.title: Checking a payment mark
events.text: A household payment is questioned. You find the mark recording the earlier payment and settle the mistake without paying again.

events.title: A split bag
events.text: A bag splits on the way home. You borrow a bowl from a nearby stall, gather what you can and return the bowl before supper.

events.title: A cart blocks the lane
events.text: A cart with a damaged wheel blocks your lane. The people carrying goods pass them around it until the owner clears the way.

events.title: Washing on the line
events.text: A line holding washed clothes sags into the dust. You take the clothes down, tighten the rope and rinse the fallen pieces again.

events.title: Waiting for your turn
events.text: You arrive to collect water just as several other households do. Everyone waits while a cracked vessel is moved out of the way.

events.title: No smaller coins
events.text: A seller cannot make change for your purchase. You visit another stall for a small item and come back with a more useful set of coins.

events.title: Returning a pan
events.text: A neighbor brings back a borrowed pan with food still in it. You share the food and remember to return their bowl the next day.

events.title: A loaf for tomorrow
events.text: A loaf has gone too dry to eat on its own. You soften pieces in a bowl rather than throw it away.

events.title: A reed catches your foot
events.text: A loose reed is sticking out of the sleeping mat. You trim it and turn the worn edge toward the wall.

events.title: The seller has moved
events.text: You go to the usual place for a purchase and find a different seller. Someone points you to the stall you were looking for.

events.title: Room on the bench
events.text: A visitor arrives while the room is being used for work. You clear a place on a bench and move the tools back after they leave.

events.title: More onions than planned
events.text: A household purchase turns out larger than expected. You swap part of it with a neighbor before the food spoils.

events.title: A rattling shutter
events.text: A shutter keeps knocking in the wind. You find its loose pin and secure it with a small wooden wedge.

events.title: A dark stair
events.text: You pause at an unlit stair until someone brings a lamp. The wait is shorter than feeling your way down with a full basket.

events.title: Keeping flies off the food
events.text: You spend part of a meal chasing flies away. Before the next meal, you find a cloth wide enough to cover the serving bowl.

events.title: A shorter round of errands
events.text: You combine two nearby errands and leave the farther one for another day. The household still has what it needs for supper.

events.title: Moving the seat
events.text: You move a seat nearer the doorway for better light. Someone objects to the narrow passage, and you find a place that suits you both.

events.title: Explaining the recipe
events.text: A younger person asks how you prepare a familiar dish. You give the quantities, then have to explain what you mean by a small handful.

events.title: A lid for an old jar
events.text: The lid of an old storage jar no longer fits well. You test two others before finding one that keeps the contents covered.

events.title: The visitor is late
events.text: A visitor arrives long after the agreed time. You have already eaten, so you put out a small plate while they explain the delay.

events.title: Trying a nearer shop
events.text: You try a shop closer to home. The choice is smaller, but the shorter walk makes it useful for ordinary purchases.

events.title: Sorting a tangle of cord
events.text: You sit down with a tangled bundle of cord. By the time someone asks for a length, you have enough of it untangled to help.

events.title: The streets have changed
events.text: You give someone directions, then remember that a passage has been closed. You call them back before they turn the corner.

events.title: Something from an old household task
events.text: You find a small item left from an old household task. You explain what it was used for before putting it back with the other things.

events.title: Taking the lighter basket
events.text: Two baskets need carrying. You take the lighter one and agree where to meet the person carrying the other.

events.title: Listening at the doorway
events.text: You sit by the doorway while people discuss a delivery. You recognize the place they mention and settle a disagreement about the route.

events.title: A useful measure
events.text: A household measure has lost its handle. You show someone which unbroken cup can hold the same amount until it is repaired.

events.title: Balancing the load
events.text: A load keeps slipping to one side. You stop, move the packing and ask another porter to check it before setting off.

events.title: An unclear cargo mark
events.text: Two bundles have similar cargo marks. You leave them apart until the person receiving the delivery identifies the right one.

events.title: Pots drying too quickly
events.text: The edges of a fresh clay piece are drying faster than its base. You cover part of it and return to check it later.

events.title: Finding space for the firing
events.text: You rearrange a group of dry pots so they will fit the available kiln space. A narrow piece needs a place of its own.

events.title: Following the wood grain
events.text: A cut starts to lift a splinter along the wood grain. You turn the piece and work back from the other direction.

events.title: Matching two fittings
events.text: Two wooden fittings are meant to match. You set them side by side and remove a little more from the uneven one.

events.title: Checking the relief in daylight
events.text: A shallow line in the stone disappears when you move the lamp. You check the relief in daylight before deciding whether it needs another cut.

events.title: A total checked twice
events.text: You check a column of quantities and get two different totals. A line was counted twice; you correct it before the record is handed over.

events.title: Keeping a sheet dry
events.text: Water reaches the edge of the workbench. You lift the written sheet clear and dry the bench before continuing the copy.

events.title: Moving the display
events.text: A doorway display keeps getting knocked by people passing. You move it farther inside and leave more room to enter.

events.title: A coil out of place
events.text: A loose coil of rope is lying where the crew walks. You put it away before the next load comes aboard.

events.title: Waiting ashore
events.text: The crew is ready before the cargo is. You wait ashore and check the bundles when the last delivery finally arrives.

events.title: A different example
events.text: A learner cannot follow an argument. You try an example about buying bread, and they can finally explain the point back to you.

events.title: A line copied out of place
events.text: A copied sky table has one line shifted into the wrong column. You compare it with the source and mark where the copy must be corrected.

events.title: A client asks again
events.text: A client asks you to repeat part of a traditional chart interpretation. You explain what the reading claims and where you cannot give a definite answer.

events.title: Checking the kit
events.text: You spread out your equipment and replace a worn fastening. Another soldier points out a strap you had missed.

events.title: The supply tally
events.text: The supply tally does not match the delivered bundles. You have the bundles opened and counted before accepting the delivery.

events.title: Waiting outside the meeting
events.text: A meeting runs late. You compare notes with another attendant and check which papers you will need when called inside.

events.title: A visit cut short
events.text: You meet the person you are courting, but a household errand cuts the visit short. You agree on another time before leaving.

events.title: A small thing remembered
events.text: The person you are courting brings something you mentioned needing. You had forgotten the conversation, but they had remembered it.

events.title: Keeping supper warm
events.text: One of you comes home late. The other keeps part of supper covered, and you catch up while the dishes are put away.

events.title: Making room for two tasks
events.text: You and your spouse both need the same work surface. You move one task to a tray and finish without another argument.

events.title: Another question
events.text: A child in your household asks why the moon does not look the same every night. You watch it together and answer what you can.

events.title: Sandals left in the way
events.text: A child leaves sandals where everyone walks. After someone trips over them, you find a place where the child can put them each day.

events.title: Help without being asked
events.text: One of your children helps put away the meal without being asked. The job goes faster, though a bowl ends up on the wrong shelf.

events.title: A bundle returned
events.text: After the separation, a bundle of your things reaches your household. You check it and send back an item that belongs to your former spouse.

events.title: A place at someone else's meal
events.text: A neighbor invites you to a meal with their household. You bring a small contribution and stay to help clear the dishes.

events.title: News carried by a relative
events.text: A relative brings household news from across the city. You ask them to take a short reply when they next visit.

events.title: A jar breaks on your errand
events.text: A small empty jar slips from your hands. Nobody saw it fall, and the household will ask where it is.

choices.text: Tell the household what happened

outcomes.text: You show the broken pieces. An adult helps you clear them and sends you with an unbroken jar next time.

choices.text: Ask someone to show you a repair

outcomes.text: The jar will not hold water again, but a worker shows you how to secure the pieces for another use.

choices.text: Hide the pieces for now

outcomes.text: The missing jar is noticed. You have to explain the breakage and why you hid it.

events.title: An argument over the game
events.text: The children disagree about where the playing area ends. The argument is taking longer than the game.

choices.text: Draw clear lines and start again

outcomes.text: You draw new boundaries where everyone can see them. The game starts over with less arguing.

choices.text: Ask each child to explain their rule

outcomes.text: You hear several different rules. The group agrees on one version for this afternoon.

choices.text: Find something else to do

outcomes.text: You leave the game and spend the afternoon near home. The others are still arguing when you pass later.

events.title: The water is too heavy
events.text: You are asked to carry a small water jar. It is full enough that you keep spilling some as you walk.

choices.text: Ask for a smaller load

outcomes.text: An adult pours some water into another vessel. You carry the lighter jar home without losing more.

choices.text: Ask another child to carry it with you

outcomes.text: You and another child hold the jar between you. You have to agree on each turn, but the water reaches home.

choices.text: Carry it slowly on your own

outcomes.text: You stop several times to change hands. By the time you arrive, the jar is lighter and your arms are tired.

events.title: Clay left on the bench
events.text: A potter lets you use a little leftover clay while an adult watches. There is time for one small piece.

choices.text: Try shaping a tiny cup

outcomes.text: You pinch up the sides of a small cup. The rim is uneven, and the potter shows you where you made it too thin.

choices.text: Make counters for a game

outcomes.text: You roll the clay into small counters and press a mark into each one. The other children help you count them.

choices.text: Watch the potter instead

outcomes.text: You leave the clay alone and watch how the potter keeps the sides of a vessel even.

events.title: Part of the message is missing
events.text: Halfway through an errand, you realize you cannot remember the end of the message.

choices.text: Go back and ask again

outcomes.text: The sender repeats the message. You say it back before setting off a second time.

choices.text: Ask a familiar adult to come with you

outcomes.text: A familiar adult walks back with you and helps you check the message before you deliver it.

choices.text: Deliver only the part you remember

outcomes.text: The recipient has questions you cannot answer. An adult must make another trip to put the message right.

events.title: Your measurements do not match
events.text: You help measure a length of material. Your result differs from the worker checking it.

choices.text: Measure it together from the same end

outcomes.text: You had started from a different mark. Measuring together shows where the difference came from.

choices.text: Practise marking a spare piece

outcomes.text: You practise on a spare piece until the marks line up with the worker's measure.

choices.text: Let the worker finish the measuring

outcomes.text: The worker finishes the measurements while you clear the space for the next task.

events.title: A small payment of your own
events.text: You receive 5 drachmas for a completed errand. Someone at home asks what you plan to do with it.

choices.text: Keep the 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You put the payment away and check where you have stored it before leaving the room.

choices.text: Use the payment for a shared meal

outcomes.text: You bring home food bought with the errand payment. There is a little more to share at supper.

choices.text: Trade the payment for help with numbers

outcomes.text: A worker spends time checking simple sums with you in exchange for the payment.

events.title: A delivery before closing
events.text: Someone offers you 5 drachmas to deliver a small parcel before a nearby shop closes. It will use the time you meant to spend practising.

choices.text: Make the delivery for 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You arrive before the shop closes and bring back the acknowledgment. The sender pays you 5 drachmas.

choices.text: Keep the time for tool practice

outcomes.text: Someone else takes the parcel. You use the time to practise making a clean cut under a worker's eye.

choices.text: Ask a friend to make the trip with you

outcomes.text: Your friend helps you finish the delivery. You share the payment and spend it together on food.

events.title: A chipped measuring cup
events.text: A measuring cup has a chipped rim. You are about to use it for a household purchase.

choices.text: Borrow an unbroken measure

outcomes.text: You borrow a sound measure and check the purchase with it before returning it.

choices.text: Ask how much the damage changes it

outcomes.text: A worker compares the damaged cup with another. You learn why filling it to the chipped rim gives a different amount.

choices.text: Take it back and ask for another

outcomes.text: The household gives you another cup. The errand takes longer, but there is no argument about the quantity.

events.title: A customer you cannot understand
events.text: A customer asks a question in words you do not follow. They point at the goods and begin again.

choices.text: Find someone who understands them

outcomes.text: A nearby worker explains the request. You stay to hear the answer and recognize a few words the next time.

choices.text: Show the goods and check by gesture

outcomes.text: You set out the possible items and let the customer indicate what they need. A worker checks before anything is sold.

choices.text: Leave the request to an experienced worker

outcomes.text: An experienced worker takes over while you return to the task you were doing.

events.title: Room for a neighbor's goods
events.text: A neighbor asks to keep a few dry baskets in your household's storage space for a short time.

choices.text: Make room without charging

outcomes.text: You move your household's baskets together and make space. The neighbor collects everything on the agreed day.

choices.text: Agree on a 5-drachma storage payment

outcomes.text: You agree on which baskets can stay and for how long. The neighbor pays 5 drachmas when collecting them.

choices.text: Keep the space for your own household

outcomes.text: The neighbor finds another place. You keep the storage area ready for your own deliveries.

events.title: Too much change
events.text: After a purchase, you find that the seller returned 5 drachmas more than you were owed.

choices.text: Return the extra coins

outcomes.text: You go back and show the seller the mistake. They check the payment and thank you.

choices.text: Keep the extra coins

outcomes.text: You put the extra coins away. On a later visit, the seller questions the earlier payment.

events.title: The wrong bundle arrives
events.text: A delivery to your household contains goods meant for someone else. The person who brought it has already left.

choices.text: Find the carrier and exchange the bundle

outcomes.text: You find the carrier before the next delivery is unloaded. The two bundles are exchanged.

choices.text: Ask a reader to check the delivery mark

outcomes.text: A reader identifies the household named on the bundle. You take it there and ask where your own delivery went.

choices.text: Keep it aside for the carrier's return

outcomes.text: You leave the bundle unopened. The carrier comes back after the other household notices the mistake.

events.title: A repair does not hold
events.text: A customer returns a small wooden fitting you repaired. The joint has opened, and they want you to put it right.

choices.text: Redo the joint without another charge

outcomes.text: You take the joint apart and make a better fit. The customer checks it before leaving.

choices.text: Return 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You return 5 drachmas and take the fitting back. You examine the failed joint before deciding whether to reuse the wood.

choices.text: Ask a more experienced worker to inspect it

outcomes.text: The worker points out where the wood was split. You explain the fault to the customer and agree on a replacement.

events.title: A relative wants help at a stall
events.text: A relative is trying a small market stall and asks you to help for an afternoon.

choices.text: Help without taking a share

outcomes.text: You watch the goods while your relative handles customers. They finish the afternoon with the stock in order.

choices.text: Check the stock and payment records

outcomes.text: You help count the remaining goods and match the payments. A missed entry explains the uneven total.

choices.text: Keep the time for your own household

outcomes.text: Your relative finds other help. You finish the tasks already waiting at home.

events.title: A joint purchase of grain
events.text: Several neighbors want to combine a grain purchase. Your share would cost 10 drachmas and needs someone to check the quantities.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas and help divide it

outcomes.text: You contribute 10 drachmas and help measure each household's share. Everyone leaves with the agreed amount.

choices.text: Help check the measure without joining
